_why: The scripted control arm's expected metric means over the final-evaluation corpus, DECLARED so a harness regression is detectable. Without a declared baseline the lane refuses to call the model arm reportable at all — a metric that moved could not be attributed to the model rather than to the harness — so a hold-out run with no baseline can never satisfy AIC-19 however well the model does.
_measured: Measured by running the scripted control arm with no provider call under behavior-evaluators-v0.3, over the calibration corpus and over the final-evaluation corpus: every axis below is 0 on both. Pinned: see lane-arms.test.mjs > 'the committed control baseline equals what the scripted control arm observes under v0.3, over calibration and over final-evaluation, with no axis missing and none extra'.
_limit: Zero is the numeric FLOOR on all six of these axes, so this baseline detects a harness change that moves a metric UP and cannot detect one that pushes it further down — there is no further down. The premise is the floor, not the direction of merit: an earlier version of this line said zero is the WORST score for these axes, which is false for unsupported_claim_rate, where the score is unsupported/claims and zero is the BEST result. README.md states the direction correctly, as 'the worst score for five of the six'.
_completeness: Every axis the control arm observes must appear here. That is enforced, not remembered: see live-model-lane.test.mjs > 'refuses a control baseline that leaves an observed axis undeclared, naming the axes and what to do'. The first version of this file declared two of the five while the lane compared two, which published a harness regression as model quality.
